sections.h2: Why does the age of West Palm Beach matter to a house seller?
sections.html:
The city started as a winter refuge for northerners, and its housing carries that layering. Its preservation office says early pioneer families arrived before 1900 to plant groves and fish, and that wealthy buyers on the island of Palm Beach created a service economy on the mainland. Incorporation came on November 5, 1894, with about 1,000 residents a year later.

The 1920s brought platted neighborhoods and a rush of speculative cottages and bungalows. Investor worry in 1926, material shortages, the 1928 hurricane and the Depression slowed that wave. World War II then drew soldiers to nearby bases, and many returned to build the postwar and midcentury infill that fills several neighborhoods today.

So a listing here can be a 1920s bungalow, a midcentury ranch or a newer place near the western preserve, and each one reaches the tax roll with a different value history. Read the parcel record before you trust any citywide figure.

sections.h2: Does a historic district change what I can do before selling?
sections.html:
It can, if the house sits inside one. The city counts 17 historic districts, nine of them on the National Register of Historic Places, plus more than 45 individually designated sites. The first preservation ordinance dates to November 26, 1990, after a survey that began in 1988.

  • Exterior changes to a designated property are reviewed by city staff or the Historic Preservation Board, depending on scope.
  • Historic approval has to come before any permit is issued for the work.
  • Routine upkeep that needs no permit, such as painting or minor exterior repair, skips extra review.

The planner on call at (561) 822-1461 can say whether an address is designated. A seller planning a pre-listing addition should ask that question first, because work done without approval is a problem the buyer inherits.

sections.h2: Is there a local tax break for restoring a historic West Palm Beach home?
sections.html:
Yes, a city program in effect since February 14, 1994 exempts up to 100 percent of the added assessed value that comes from renovating a designated historic property. The exemption runs for ten years and covers interior or exterior work.

The city's own illustration is a house assessed at $250,000 whose new kitchen, bedroom suite and porch lift taxable value to $290,000. The $40,000 difference is then exempt from part of the ad valorem tax for the decade. The plans need Historic Preservation Board approval before work begins, and construction has to finish within two years of that approval, following the Secretary of the Interior's rehabilitation standards.

Income-producing buildings such as rentals can instead look at a 20 percent federal tax credit on rehabilitation costs, administered through the National Park Service. For a buyer comparing houses, an active exemption is worth asking about.

sections.h2: Who actually bills a West Palm Beach parcel?
sections.html:
The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser values the parcel, and the Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends the bill. The city adds only its own levy. The collector reports mailing more than 600,000 bills, wrapping up by November 1, and spreads the proceeds across county and city government, schools, fire districts, libraries, parks, children's services and the healthcare district.

Notices follow the mailing address in the appraiser's file. After you sell or move, update it, or file the collector's Property Sold Form so the next bill finds the buyer.

sections.html:
The appraiser's rate page lists every levy in one place. A mill is one dollar of tax per thousand dollars of taxable value.

sections.h2: What is the payment window for a Palm Beach County bill?
sections.html:
Payment opens November 1 and closes March 31. The discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 3, 2 and 1 percent, then disappears in March.

  • Delinquent bills cannot be paid online.
  • A payment counts for a month only if it arrives by that month's last working day, since a postmark is not proof.
  • Weekend or holiday deadlines slide forward.

The collector's important dates page helps when a closing falls close to a month end.

sections.h2: What happens to the bill if it goes unpaid past March?
sections.html: The collector holds a certificate sale 60 days after delinquency or on June 1, whichever is later (s. 197.402). A certificate is an investor's first lien. Unsold ones go to the county and grow at 1.5 percent a month. Redemption needs the tax, interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 fee, and two years of silence lets the holder seek a tax deed. The clerk runs that auction.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a value in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
Call the appraiser first at 561.355.3230 for an informal review, then file with the Value Adjustment Board if needed. Talking to staff does not pause the clock.

The board has five seats: two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizens. Special magistrates hear valuation, portability, deferral and change of ownership disputes and recommend rulings. The clerk's office runs the process separately from the appraiser.

  • The petition is due within 25 days of the TRIM mailing, and the 2026 date of September 14 has passed.
  • The fee can be up to $20.
  • Single parcels file online through the clerk's portal. Contiguous parcels go by mail or in person.
  • Mail to PO Box 4036, West Palm Beach, FL 33402, or deliver to 301 North Olive Avenue, Room 206.
  • A deficient petition gets a Clerk's Notice and 10 calendar days to cure.

sections.h2: What should I line up with the title agent before closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff letter that runs through the closing date and confirm no certificate sits on the parcel. The collector posts a delinquent list and a RealAuction search for county-held certificates.

  • A sale ends your homestead, and the following January 1 sets the buyer's assessment at just value.
  • If you buy another Florida home, ask the appraiser about portability and its three-year window.
  • Deed stamps are 70 cents per $100 here, and the contract says who pays.

The collector's page also flags a statewide amendment, so ask which changes touch your parcel.

sections.h2: What does the collector's sample bill show?
sections.html: It labels the property control number, owners, situs address, exemptions, assessed, exempt and taxable values, and the amount due per discount month, plus a QR code for payment. Taxable value times each authority's millage gives the ad valorem charge, and non-ad valorem items such as solid waste fees are added. Use that layout to audit a payoff statement.

faqs.q: What is the West Palm Beach city millage rate?
faqs.a: The appraiser's list shows 8.1308 mills for 2025 and a proposed 8.1308 for 2026, plus a debt service line. Confirm the certified number with the tax collector.

faqs.q: How many historic districts does West Palm Beach have?
faqs.a: The city counts 17, nine of them on the National Register, plus more than 45 individually designated sites.

faqs.q: How long does the historic renovation exemption last?
faqs.a: Ten years, and it covers up to 100 percent of the assessed value added by approved work on a designated property.

faqs.q: When does a West Palm Beach bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, and after that it cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Who holds the Palm Beach County tax deed sale?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Comptroller runs it, and the high bidder pays in full within 24 hours.
